overall: The AG found no Open Meeting Law violation: with two vacancies the Commission had five serving members, and whether three present was a quorum did not matter because either no deliberation occurred or it occurred at a properly posted meeting.

allegations.summary: Complainant alleged the March 5, 2013 meeting proceeded with only three of seven members present, short of a quorum.
allegations.key_passage: Either the Commission did not have a quorum present and therefore did not engage in deliberation, or it did have a quorum present and it deliberated during a properly posted open meeting.

allegations.summary: Complainant alleged the April 16, 2013 meeting proceeded with only three of seven members present, short of a quorum.
allegations.key_passage: Regardless, we need not determine whether the three Commission members present at its March 5, 2013 and April 16, 2013 meetings constituted a quorum because, either way, the Commission did not violate the Open Meeting Law.

note: Read by a language model from the letter; every key passage is checked verbatim against it and dropped if not. A holding is the Attorney General’s reading of the law in this case only.
